steps.label: A rise in pCO₂
steps.why: Tissues that are working hard make more carbon dioxide, and that is exactly where the blood should let go of its oxygen.
common_mistakes: Writing that a rise in pCO₂ increases the affinity. It decreases it.
Answering only one half. Both directions are asked.
steps.memory_tip: More carbon dioxide means oxygen is released at the tissues.
steps.margin_note: One line each way. Keep the contrast clear.
lines: A rise in pCO₂ decreases the affinity of

steps.label: A fall in pCO₂
steps.why: At the alveoli the carbon dioxide leaves the blood, so the same rule run backwards makes the blood pick oxygen up.
common_mistakes: Writing the same effect for both directions.
Leaving out where each change happens.
steps.memory_tip: Less carbon dioxide at the lungs means oxygen is picked up.
steps.margin_note: Say where it happens: the alveoli.
lines: A fall in pCO₂ increases the affinity of
haemoglobin for oxygen, so oxygen is taken
